verdict.rationale: Lovable's documented Build mode is a built-in autonomous agent. Users hand it a task and it 'takes ownership of execution end to end', applying changes directly with visible diffs and summaries. Users can steer it mid-task, have it run project actions like publishing or deploying from chat, and it can spin up read-only subagents for research and review. Community posts confirm people use Lovable heavily to generate apps, but none hands-on evaluates the delegation workflow itself. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of task delegation, and detail on the limits of autonomous execution (e.g. approval gates, failure handling).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: When you give Lovable a task, it takes ownership of execution end to end.
Lovable working on a request doesn't block you. Send a follow-up, a correction, or a new idea at any time to steer the work
you can also ask Lovable to run project actions from chat, for example publish my app, deploy this project, ship it, or find me a domain for my bakery
Lovable can start temporary, read-only subagents to research, inspect, or review focused parts of the work.
Lovable applies changes directly to your project when using Build mode. All modifications are visible through file diffs and summaries.
